summary: SSO sign-in verifies the identity provider's id_token (signature, issuer, audience, expiry, nonce), binds it to the authorization request with a nonce, and derives identity from verified claims with a Microsoft oid/Graph-id cross-check so existing accounts are not re-keyed. OAuth token-endpoint client authentication is configurable per provider (client_secret_post, client_secret_basic, or private_key_jwt with an encrypted, write-only key).

evidence: Agent-drafted disposition for a draft PR; maintainer review and approval are intentionally not claimed. Focused unit and e2e SSO/OAuth tests pass (66) with real RS256 fixtures covering bad signature, wrong issuer, wrong audience, expired, nonce mismatch, unknown kid, client-auth request shapes and subject cross-checks.
